text:
Leo: Hi all, Leo here. Fresh account. Quick bootstrapping snag: using Windows 11 + WSL2 + VSCode devcontainer. Followed onboarding dotfiles (asdf for node/python). Inside container, `ssh -T git@github.com` fails with Permission denied (publickey) but works in WSL. Also asdf python packages installed with pip end up in ~/.local and VSCode doesn't pick up the interpreter. Anyone seen this pattern?

Nina (devex): welcome! :wave: For the SSH part, it's almost always agent socket not forwarded. On Win -> WSL the OpenSSH agent is a named pipe; WSL exposes it at /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock on newer builds. Mount that socket into the container and set SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Example runArgs: -v /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock:/ssh-agent -e SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent.

Raj (infra): if /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock is missing, use npiperelay to proxy the Windows pipe into a unix socket in WSL, then mount. Or run ssh-agent in WSL and add key there, then mount that socket. Also check private key permissions if you mounted ~/.ssh read-only.

Leo: I tried mounting /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock and restarted the container. Now `echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` shows /ssh-agent and ssh works. For the python/vscode issue, I created a repo .venv and added a .envrc to auto-activate it; that made VSCode detect the venv.

Nina (devex): perfect. If you can, add a short note to the onboarding dotfiles README about the npiperelay/socket step for Windows folks.

bot-deploy: dotfiles-skel applied to /home/leo :white_check_mark:

Leo: will open a tiny PR, thanks everyone!
